newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's economy catches fire in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's economy catches fire in second quarter.

text.p: Mexico's economy caught fire in the second quarter, as gross domestic product grew a sharp 8.8 percent, the best quarterly performance since 1981, the government said Monday.
Economists said strength in the service sector shows the recovery is starting to deepen on the domestic side after the recession that started with the peso crash of 1994.

"The number (of 8.8 percent year-over-year) was a lot stronger than expected basically due to the services sector, which showed a surprisingly strong performance," said Santander Investment economist Enrique Ramirez.
The services sector, which includes hotels, retail sales, financial services, and transportation, posted a muscular 7.7 percent increase in the second quarter.
"It is very positive that much of the growth was due to the domestic economy and not just to exports as before," Ramirez said.

Exports were the backbone of economic growth after the peso crash allowed Mexican exporters to rapidly bump up sales abroad. But Mexican consumers have been slower to climb out of a hole of high inflation and interest rates, and lower real wages caused by the crisis.

The industrial sector rose a strong 11.2 percent in the second quarter over the same quarter a year earlier, while the agriculture sector posted a good 10.4 percent hike on strong harvests of various products, the government said.
Analysts welcomed the broadening of growth.
"The GDP number was well above expectations and helps confirm that the expansion and the recovery has broadened out," said Bankers Trust economist Denis Parisien.
A Reuters survey of brokerages and economists had shown expectations of growth closer to 6 percent in the quarter.

"It was an excellent result. The implication is very clear and that is that private consumption is stronger than many people thought," said Alonso Cervera, chief economist at brokerage house Interacciones.
The government also said first-half GDP rose 7.0 percent against the same period a year earlier.
Economists said, however, that since the Easter holiday fell in the first quarter this year, that cut into growth in the first three months but added to the second quarter strength.
Discounting the Easter effect, second-quarter GDP rose a still strong 7.4 percent, the government said.

Economists said the strong number will likely cause an increase in forecasts for annual growth, with Interacciones's Cervera saying a GDP number for the year of more than 6.0 percent would be "the most likely scenerio."
Santander Investment's Ramirez said his company, which had forecast of 5.0 percent growth for the year, could bump their number. He said an increase to 5.7 or 5.8 percent is possible.
Government officials have previously said they expect growth of about 4.5 percent in the year.
